stem: A nurse is caring for four clients with different diagnoses. Which statement best describes when Standard Precautions apply?

options.A: Use Standard Precautions only when infection is known or suspected, adding Transmission-Based Precautions if the organism requires them.
options.B: Use Standard Precautions only for tasks with anticipated blood or body-fluid exposure, not for routine bedside care.
options.C: Use Standard Precautions routinely in inpatient units, while outpatient settings rely mainly on diagnosis-specific precautions.
options.D: Use Standard Precautions for every client in every healthcare setting, including hand hygiene and task-based PPE selected according to anticipated exposure.

rationale: CDC Core Infection Prevention and Control Practices state that Standard Precautions apply to all patient care, regardless of suspected or confirmed infectious status, and across all healthcare settings. They include hand hygiene and selection of PPE based on the nature of the interaction and the anticipated risk of exposure to blood, body fluids, infectious material, mucous membranes, non-intact skin, or contaminated equipment. Transmission-Based Precautions are added when indicated; they do not replace Standard Precautions.
educational_objective: Apply Standard Precautions to every patient in every healthcare setting and select PPE according to the anticipated exposure risk for the task.
source_organization: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC)

source_original.stem: A nurse is caring for four clients with different diagnoses. Which statement best describes when Standard Precautions apply?

options.A: Use Standard Precautions when infection is known or suspected, then add Transmission-Based Precautions if the organism requires them.
options.B: Use Standard Precautions for tasks with anticipated blood or body-fluid exposure, but not for routine noninvasive bedside care.
options.C: Use Standard Precautions routinely in inpatient units, while outpatient settings rely mainly on diagnosis-specific precautions.
options.D: Use them for every client, selecting hand hygiene and task-based PPE according to anticipated exposure.

source_original.rationale: Standard Precautions are the baseline infection-prevention practices for every patient regardless of known infection status. They include hand hygiene and a task-specific risk assessment for gloves, gown, mask and eye/face protection based on anticipated exposure to blood, body fluids, mucous membranes, nonintact skin, or contaminated material.
source_original.source_detail: CDC Core Infection Prevention and Control Practices — Standard Precautions: apply to all patients in all healthcare settings; hand hygiene and task/risk-based PPE are baseline measures. correction_summary: Retained the construct and key. Tightened distractor A to remove partial-truth ambiguity and made D explicitly match CDC's 'all patient care/all settings' scope. Added the relationship that Transmission-Based Precautions supplement rather than replace Standard Precautions.

audit_findings.clinical_category: Standard Precautions — scope and PPE selection
audit_findings.currentness: CDC page dated April 12, 2024 remains current and was rechecked 2026-08-16.
audit_findings.exact_locator: Standard Precautions/5a/PPE recommendations directly support all-patient/all-setting scope and task-based PPE.
audit_findings.claim_audit: No diagnosis-specific exception or setting limitation is introduced.

distractor_audit.A: Incorrect because it limits Standard Precautions to known/suspected infection.
distractor_audit.B: Incorrect because Standard Precautions are not limited to visibly high-exposure tasks.
distractor_audit.C: Incorrect because Standard Precautions apply across healthcare settings, not inpatient only.
distractor_audit.D: Directly matches CDC and is uniquely correct.

audit_findings.ambiguity_second_answer: Only D accurately states both universal scope and task-based PPE selection.
audit_findings.cueing: All options are scope statements of similar form; no key-by-length or numeric cue.
audit_findings.blueprint: Directly maps to NCSBN Standard Precautions content.
audit_findings.independent_second_pass: Confirmed A no longer contains a partially correct formulation that could compete with D.
